options.label: YYYY-MM-DD
options.rule: When writing dates, use YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2025-04-23.

options.label: Write out year, month, and day in Hangul
options.rule: When writing dates, write out “year,” “month,” and “day” in Hangul, starting with the year. Example: 2025년 4월 23일.

options.label: YYYY. MM. DD.
options.rule: When writing dates, use YYYY. MM. DD. Example: 2025. 4. 25.

options.label: YYYY/MM/DD
options.rule: When writing dates, use YYYY/MM/DD. Example: 2025/04/23.

options.label: Use the 12-hour clock with a colon
options.rule: When writing about times of the day, use the 12-hour clock and write time with Arabic numerals and a colon. Examples: 오전 06:00; 오후 07:30.

options.label: Use the 12-hour clock with 시 and 분
options.rule: When writing about times of the day, use the 12-hour clock and write “hours” (시) and “minutes” (분) in Hangul. Examples: 오전 6시; 오후 7시 30분.

options.label: Use the 24-hour clock with a colon
options.rule: When writing about times of the day, use the 24-hour clock and write time with Arabic numerals and a colon. Examples: 06:00; 19:30.

options.label: Use the 24-hour clock with 시 and 분
options.rule: When writing about times of the day, use the 24-hour clock and write “hours” (시) and “minutes” (분) in Hangul. Examples: 6시; 19시 30분.

options.label: Spell out the word in Hangul after the amount
options.rule: When writing currencies, spell out the word in Hangul after the amount. Examples: 5000원; 100달러.

options.label: Use the currency symbol before the amount
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the currency symbol before the amount. Examples: ₩5000; $100.

options.label: Use the ISO code before the amount
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the ISO code before the amount. Examples: KRW 5000; USD 100.

options.label: Use only Arabic numerals
options.rule: When writing large numbers, use only Arabic numerals. Example: 125000.

options.label: Use 만, 억, 조 with a space
options.rule: When writing large numbers, use Hangul for “million,” “billion,” and “trillion” (만, 억, 조) with a space. Example: 12만 5000.

options.label: Use 만, 억, 조 without a space
options.rule: When writing large numbers, use Hangul for “million,” “billion,” and “trillion” without a space. Example: 12만5000.

options.label: Don’t use
options.rule: For thousands separators, don’t use them. Example: 125000.

options.label: Use
options.rule: For thousands separators, use them. Example: 125,000.

options.label: Use Hangul without a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use Hangul for “percent” without a space. Example: 70퍼센트.

options.label: Use % without a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use % without a space. Example: 70%.

options.label: Use Hangul with a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use Hangul for “percent” with a space. Example: 70 퍼센트.

options.label: Use % with a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use % with a space. Example: 70 %.

options.label: Spell out units in Korean
options.rule: For units of measure, spell out units in Korean instead of using symbols. Example: 100 제곱미터.

options.label: Use SI symbols
options.rule: For units of measure, use SI symbols. Example: 100 ㎡.

options.label: Don’t use spaces
options.rule: Between unit nouns and numbers, don’t use spaces. Example: 10명.

options.label: Use spaces
options.rule: Between unit nouns and numbers, use spaces. Example: 10 명.

options.label: Spell out the full unit
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals for the measure but spell out the full unit. Examples: 섭씨 100도; 화씨 32도; 0캘빈.

options.label: Use numerals followed by 도
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals followed by the word “degrees” (도). Example: 100도.

options.label: Use the unit symbol with a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals followed by the unit symbol, with a space. Examples: 100 ℃; 32 ℉; 273.16 K.

options.label: Use the unit symbol without a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals followed by the unit symbol, without a space. Examples: 100℃; 32℉; 273.16K.

options.label: Don’t use spaces before or after a colon for time, verses, versus, or to
options.rule: Don’t use spaces before or after a colon when separating hours and minutes or chapters and verses, or when it is used to mean “versus” or “to.” Examples: 오전 11:30; 요한복음 3:5; 한국과 일본은 0:0으로 경기를 마쳤다.

options.label: Use a space after a colon in a heading
options.rule: Use a space after a colon in a heading but not before it. Example: 일시: 2025년 10월 10일.

options.label: Don’t use
options.rule: After conjunctive adverbs, don’t use a comma. Example: 그런데 나는....

options.label: Use
options.rule: After conjunctive adverbs, use a comma. Example: 그런데, 나는....

options.label: Use six dots at the bottom
options.rule: When using ellipses, use six dots at the bottom (......).

options.label: Use six dots in the center
options.rule: When using ellipses, use six dots in the center (⋯⋯).

options.label: Use three dots at the bottom
options.rule: When using ellipses, use three dots at the bottom (...).

options.label: Use three dots in the center
options.rule: When using ellipses, use three dots in the center (⋯).

rules.title: Parentheses
examples: 소크라테스(고대 그리스의 철학자)의 말을 빌리면 다음과 같다.
rules.rule: When using parentheses to provide supplementary information for a word or phrase, attach them directly to the surrounding words without spaces. Example: 소크라테스(고대 그리스의 철학자)의 말을 빌리면 다음과 같다.

options.label: Don’t use
options.rule: For periods in a quote, don’t use them. Example: 그는 “오늘은 정말 좋은 날이야”라고 말했다.

options.label: Use
options.rule: For periods in a quote, use them. Example: 그는 “오늘은 정말 좋은 날이야.”라고 말했다.

options.label: Curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use curly (“...”) quotation marks.

options.label: Straight quotation marks
options.rule: Use straight ("...") quotation marks.

options.label: Use double for primary and single for secondary quotations
options.rule: Use double for primary quotation marks and single for secondary quotation marks.

options.label: Use a hyphen
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use a hyphen (-). Examples: 9월 15일-9월 25일; 서울-천안 정도는 출퇴근이 가능하다.

options.label: Use 부터…까지
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use “부터…까지” (“from...to”). Example: 9월 15일부터 9월 25일까지.

options.label: Use a tilde
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use a tilde (~). Examples: 9월 15일~9월 25일; 서울~천안 정도는 출퇴근이 가능하다.

options.label: Use a comma
options.rule: When joining closely related words or phrases, use a comma (,). Example: 한, 일 양국 간의 무역량.

options.label: Use a hyphen
options.rule: When joining closely related words or phrases, use a hyphen (-). Example: 한-일 양국 간의 무역량.

options.label: Use a middle dot
options.rule: When joining closely related words or phrases, use a middle dot (·). Example: 한·일 양국 간의 무역량.

options.label: Use double angle brackets
options.rule: When writing the titles of books and newspapers, use double angle brackets (《...》). Example: 《훈민정음》은 1997년....

options.label: Use double corner brackets
options.rule: When writing the titles of books and newspapers, use double corner brackets (『...』). Example: 『훈민정음』은 1997년....

options.label: Use double straight quotation marks
options.rule: When writing the titles of books and newspapers, use double straight quotation marks ("..."). Example: "훈민정음"은 1997년....

options.label: Use single angle brackets
options.rule: When marking titles of creative works (subheadings, paintings, songs), as well as trade names, laws, and regulations, use single angle brackets (〈...〉). Example: 현행〈국어의 로마자 표기법〉은....

options.label: Use single corner brackets
options.rule: When marking titles of creative works (subheadings, paintings, songs), as well as trade names, laws, and regulations, use single corner brackets (「...」). Example: 현행 ｢국어의 로마자 표기법｣은....

options.label: Use single straight quotation marks
options.rule: When marking titles of creative works (subheadings, paintings, songs), as well as trade names, laws, and regulations, use single straight quotation marks ('...'). Example: 현행 '국어의 로마자 표기법'은....

options.label: Don’t use abbreviations unless necessary
options.rule: For abbreviations, don’t use abbreviations unless necessary. Example: 노동조합(O) → 노조(X).

options.label: Use abbreviations as needed
options.rule: For abbreviations, use abbreviations as needed. Example: 노동조합(O) → 노조(O).

options.label: Use active voice; use passive voice only when the agent is unknown or irrelevant
options.rule: For passive voice, use active voice; use passive voice only when the agent is unknown or irrelevant.

options.label: Use passive voice as needed
options.rule: For passive voice, use passive voice as needed.

options.label: Use as is
options.rule: For established loanwords, use them as is. Examples: 커플; 이벤트; 다이어트 등.

options.label: Use native or Sino-Korean equivalents
options.rule: For established loanwords, use native or Sino-Korean equivalents. Examples: 이슈 → 쟁점; 인프라 → 기반시설.

options.label: Paraphrase in Korean
options.rule: For unestablished loanwords, paraphrase in Korean. Example: 클리셰 전개 → 진부한 전개.

options.label: Use as is
options.rule: For unestablished loanwords, use them as is. Example: 클리셰 전개 → 클리셰 전개.

options.label: Use as is, with a brief explanation in parentheses
options.rule: For unestablished loanwords, use them as is, with a brief explanation in parentheses. Example: 클리셰 전개 → 클리셰(진부한) 전개.

options.label: Don’t use first-person pronouns
options.rule: For first-person pronouns, don’t use first-person pronouns, for a more impersonal tone.

options.label: Omit the first-person subject when clear from context
options.rule: For first-person pronouns, omit the first-person subject when it is clear from context.

options.label: Use first-person pronouns as they are
options.rule: For first-person pronouns, use first-person pronouns as they are.

options.label: Don’t use second-person pronouns
options.rule: For second-person pronouns, don’t use second-person pronouns, for a more impersonal tone. Examples: 독자; 사용자; 고객님; 선생님 등.

options.label: Use second-person pronouns as they are
options.rule: For second-person pronouns, use second-person pronouns as they are.

options.label: Mix Hapsho and Haeyo styles appropriately
examples: 일정은 아래와 같습니다. 꼭 참여해 보세요.
options.rule: For declarative endings, mix Hapsho and Haeyo styles appropriately. Example: 일정은 아래와 같습니다. 꼭 참여해 보세요.

options.label: Use the Haeyo style
examples: 일정은 아래와 같아요. 꼭 참여해 보세요.
options.rule: For declarative endings, use the Haeyo style (–어요/–해요). Example: 일정은 아래와 같아요. 꼭 참여해 보세요.

options.label: Use the Hapsho style
examples: 일정은 아래와 같습니다. 꼭 참여해 보십시오.
options.rule: For declarative endings, use the Hapsho style (–습니다/–십시오). Example: 일정은 아래와 같습니다. 꼭 참여해 보십시오.

options.label: Use the Hara style
examples: 일정은 아래와 같다. 꼭 참여해 보길 바린다.
options.rule: For declarative endings, use the Hara style (–하다/–이다). Example: 일정은 아래와 같다. 꼭 참여해 보길 바린다.
